analogy_mapping.Agent Nodes: PTT snapshot reached after each new tree item (state = cumulative tree)
analogy_mapping.Search Nodes: The PTT tree item worked on (number + title) + its MCP_tasks tool calls
analogy_mapping.Track Nodes: That item's findings payload -- what was actually discovered

node_types.Agent (Blue/Pink goal): PTT state after a new item completes
node_types.Search (Orange): PTT item being worked (tool calls in tooltip)

edge_types.StateTransition (Black): Agent -> Agent, label = PTT item number
edge_types.SearchUpdate (Green): Agent -> Search, item being worked from that state
edge_types.TrackUpdate (Blue): Search -> Track, what item's execution found
edge_types.Prediction (Purple): Track -> Agent, leads to next cumulative PTT state

1.6 Vulnerability Analysis:
1.6.1 Analyze Git version 2.45.0 - {Findings: Git version 2.45.0.windows.1 is affected by several security vulnerabilities including potential for remote code execution and unauthorized file modifications. Key vulnerabilities include: CVE-2024-32002 (Critical): Allows for remote code execution via specially crafted repositories with submodules. CVE-2024-32004: Allows an attacker to execute arbitrary code on multi-user machines via a crafted local repository. CVE-2024-32020: Could lead to hardlinked files in the target repository's object database if local source and target repositories are on the same disk. CVE-2024-32021: Allows Git to create hardlinks to arbitrary user-readable files when cloning a local source repository containing symlinks. CVE-2024-32465: Allows an attacker to bypass protections designed for cloning untrusted repositories, particularly when processing .zip files containing a full Git repository copy. These vulnerabilities primarily involve improper handling of symbolic links, case-insensitive filesystems, and untrusted repositories, particularly with submodules. Mitigation involves updating to Git for Windows 2.45.1.
